messages.subject: Combining two types of graph
parts:
Hello guys, I would like to combine the two graphs that I created and I was wondering if there is a simple way to do so or I should combine my data?


head(xmelt)
  Var1     Var2       value L1
1    2 Outright -0.28654296 DE
2    3 Outright -1.50630308 DE
3    5 Outright -2.15538949 DE
4    7 Outright -1.35790387 DE
5   10 Outright -0.48020902 DE
6   15 Outright  0.08511379 DE


p <- ggplot(xmelt, aes(x=factor(Var1),value, row=L1, col=Var2, group=Var2, fill=factor(Var1))) + 
geom_bar(stat="identity")+ facet_grid(Var2~L1, scale="free") +  
xlab("Maturities") + ylab("Basis Points Move") + theme(legend.position = "none", 
axis.text.x = element_text(size=6) ) + scale_fill_grey(start=0.8,end=0.3)



################################################################################################

       dates maturities     yields countries              L1
1 2011-07-11   4.249315 0.01718019        DE 3 years history
2 2011-07-11   4.487671 0.01756333        DE 3 years history
3 2011-07-11   4.632877 0.01797178        DE 3 years history
4 2011-07-11   4.747945 0.01830480        DE 3 years history
5 2011-07-11   4.947945 0.01909274        DE 3 years history
6 2011-07-11   4.986301 0.01875390        DE 3 years history

q <- ggplot(zz, aes(maturities, yields*100, group=dates, colour=L1)) + geom_smooth(se=F) +
geom_point(data=zz[zz$L1=="Actual curve", ], colour="brown", alpha=2/5, size=5 ) +
scale_colour_manual("Legend", values = c("3 years history" = "#B6B6B4", "63 days history" = "brown", "Actual curve" = "gold")) +
ylab("") + xlab("Maturities") + theme(legend.position = c(0.98, 0.1), legend.background = 
element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA), plot.title = element_text(lineheight=.8, face="bold")) + 
facet_wrap(~countries, ncol=7, scale="fixed")



By the way I was wondering if someone know if it would be possible to sort the country in their actual order, rather than the alphabetical order. 


Thank you for your time.

Regards,


Alex

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: Combining two types of graph
parts:
Given how dissimilar your two examples are, I assume by "combine" you mean that you want to stack them on top of each other on the same page? In that case the gridExtra package is probably the way to go. This will let you do something like

grid.arrange( p, q, nrow=2, ncol=1 )

Sorting the countries: you need to specify a different ordering of factor levels for the country field, e.g.

zz$countries <- factor( zz$countries, levels=c( "FR", "NE", ...etc ) )

Ben
